items.readable_text:
Content:
Sometimes, when adding two numbers in scientific notation, we get a number that's not in scientific notation. In such cases, we need to rewrite the final result.

Content:
To demonstrate, let's calculate the following sum:

Content:
[MATH: \left(9 \times 10^{7}\right) + \left(9.3 \times 10^{8}\right)]

Content:
The first number in the sum is the smaller of the two, so we rewrite it to have the same power of [MATH: 10] as the second number, as follows:

Content:
[MATH: 9 × 10^{7}|=; 9 × 10^{8 − 1}|=; 9 × 10^{− 1 + 8}|=; 9 × 10^{− 1} × 10^{8}; 0.9 × 10^{8}]

Content:
Now, we can carry out the addition as usual:

Content:
[MATH: (9 × 10^{7}) + (9.3 × 10^{8})|=; (0.9 × 10^{8}) + (9.3 × 10^{8})|=; (0.9 + 9.3) × 10^{8}|=; 10.2 × 10^{8}]

Content:
The above number is not in scientific notation because [MATH: 10.2 \gt 10.] So, we need to write [MATH: 10.2] in scientific notation, as follows:

Content:
[MATH: 10.2 = 1.02\times 10^{1}]

Content:
Therefore,

Content:
[MATH: 10.2 × 10^{8}|=; (1.02 × 10^{1}) × 10^{8}|=; 1.02 × (10^{1} × 10^{8})|=; 1.02 × 10^{1 + 8}|=; 1.02 × 10^{9}.]

Content:
Hence, our final answer is [MATH: 1.02 \times 10^{9}.]
